commitsSinceProduction.subject: Merge pull request #8 from floration/claude/project-thread-xq2e2m
commitsSinceProduction.author: floration

commitsSinceProduction.subject: 1.18.5: changelogs (short and full) and release checklist rows for the shipped light bakes, the refocus click and 3D sound
commitsSinceProduction.author: claude

commitsSinceProduction.subject: Audio: the IAudioClient3 declaration out of the anonymous namespace (an abstract class with no derived class in the file let GCC make every call through it unreachable: the game crashed at audio start on Windows 10+)
commitsSinceProduction.author: claude

commitsSinceProduction.subject: Shipped light bakes zlib'd: maps/lightcache/<sha256>.qlbz, 84 MB of bakes ship as 11.7 MB (qpak +11.7 MB, not +84)
commitsSinceProduction.author: claude

commitsSinceProduction.subject: Shipped light bakes: packages carry the official maps' bakes in maps/lightcache (no first-join bake: Midtown ~5 s, Lodestone ~2.8 s)
commitsSinceProduction.author: claude

commitsSinceProduction.subject: Reliable events handled in id order and acked only up to the last one with none missing (owner): a later event arriving first (the server's paced resends, a big one waiting for room) used to be acked past the missing one, which was then lost for good (kill feed, chat, names, ranked tickets, map edits); demos keep taking every newer id
commitsSinceProduction.author: claude

commitsSinceProduction.subject: Audio: shared WASAPI at the engine's shortest period (Windows 10+, IAudioClient3) in its float mix format, one period queued, where the driver allows a period under the default; the 10 ms path otherwise (or QUARK_AUDIO_LEGACY=1); QUARK_AUDIO_MS works on both; the log names the engine period and why not shorter (owner)
commitsSinceProduction.author: claude

commitsSinceProduction.subject: The click that brings the game window back (after alt-tab) no longer fires: a mouse press in the same event poll as the focus returning is swallowed, and its button isn't down until released (owner)
commitsSinceProduction.author: claude

commitsSinceProduction.subject: Client (loop 2): late mouse reads take only the motion (focus and cursor hold in the frame's first read), the screen mode cached (no display driver query per frame), ULTRA's CPU time measured before its GPU wait (pacing no longer switched itself off when GPU-bound), Latent Sync lead from the 3rd slowest of 256 frames with retried raster clock and no GPU drain when unsynced, F3 slots read in order / reset on enable / bracketed clock calibration / latch timestamp fixed, hud.cfg watched off the frame (and under non-ASCII folders), health bar rays skipped off screen and the last blocking ray tried first; fixes: alt-toggle scope zoom, recoil decay, footsteps in the air at high fps, killstreaks across matches, stray fire after Esc / a bake, remote shot origins at body scale, spectated shots visible, PLAYS AS reaching every mode, map index after a rescan, unknown console settings, lifetime polling; editor: static batch only for box edits, drags without map copies, cached per-map results, stale online selections
commitsSinceProduction.author: claude

commitsSinceProduction.subject: Light bake (loop 2): the prepass's three passes in parallel (same faces and vertices; cached Midtown load ~110 -> ~40 ms), 1 ms progress waits, cache touched on use and written atomically; glTF accessors range-checked before allocating, mismatched normal / colour counts ignored
commitsSinceProduction.author: claude

commitsSinceProduction.subject: Audio (loop 2): the game thread queues sounds and never waits for a mix pass, 3D sounds follow the listener while they play (gains ramped per period), 32.32 fixed-point mixer loop, exclusive mode also tries extensible float / 24-bit / 16-bit formats and tells busy from unsupported
commitsSinceProduction.author: claude

commitsSinceProduction.subject: Renderer and UI (loop 2): exact integer rounding for 2D quads (about 7x cheaper per glyph, same bytes), colour packed once per text / rect, translucent upload and aim-independent uniforms before the late read, uniform locations cached and constants set once, relatch only re-aims, per-frame lists reserved, static batch memory kept between rebuilds, fewer label copies in buttons / cycles / sliders
commitsSinceProduction.author: claude

commitsSinceProduction.subject: Netclient (loop 2): render bracket found without walking the whole history (interp off walked 512 snapshots a frame), the ack's prediction stored on a mismatch (no repeated full replays), O(1) findPlayer and players interpolated in place, tickRate 0 / over 1000 rejected, jitter reset per connection and eased in demos, demo records split at 255 events with ids taken only once written
commitsSinceProduction.author: claude

commitsSinceProduction.subject: 1.18.4: changelogs (short and full) for the reliable-event room fix
commitsSinceProduction.author: claude

commitsSinceProduction.subject: Snapshots: the oldest unacked reliable event, when due, always gets its room (fewer projectiles that snapshot until it fits, as for an overflowing world): the client now takes events in id order, so a big one that kept not fitting would hold back every later one (with the client change in netclient.cpp)
commitsSinceProduction.author: claude

commitsSinceProduction.subject: Tick rate test: 14 ms stalls (were 12), so 250 Hz stalls and 125 Hz doesn't whatever the stall's phase (a 12 ms stall right after a 125 Hz tick holds the next one only 4 ms: with Linux's exact sleeps 250 Hz looked clean and it stepped up; CI run 147)
commitsSinceProduction.author: claude

commitsSinceProduction.subject: 1.18.3: changelogs (short and full) and a release checklist row for the server CPU pass and the late-tick / bandwidth rate check
commitsSinceProduction.author: claude

commitsSinceProduction.subject: Server tick: lag-compensation rewind finds its record by binary search inside the contiguous history run (the walk's own checks finish it; rifle shot at 250 ms 7.7 -> 0.8 us); hit feedback walks a per-attacker bitmask instead of 32x32; no repeat reachability string with no prober. Same results (14 scenarios hashed per tick)
commitsSinceProduction.author: claude

commitsSinceProduction.subject: Visibility: a remembered blocker per (viewer, target) pair is tried first, accepted only where raycastAny's own walk would reach and hit it (exact: 2.3 billion rays compared, per-tick visibility hashes identical); the pair scan skips dead slots in bulk; visibility ~2x faster, snapbench midtown 32 97 -> 50 us
commitsSinceProduction.author: claude

commitsSinceProduction.subject: Rate check (owner): ticks held back past 2 snapshot intervals (3 ms at least) in over 1% of a window step the tick rate down whatever the CPU reads (a capped VM never stepped down); bandwidth short (--max-upload-kbps, or most players losing snapshots / ping up at once) lowers the snapshot rate first (500, 333, 250, 125/s), then the tick rate; one lossy player no longer moves the server; status shows rates, stalls, kbps and the last change's reason
commitsSinceProduction.author: claude

commitsSinceProduction.subject: Bots: per-bot cache of the tick-rate / skill constants (exp, chance thresholds, seenAgo offsets, turn steps) and an exact wrapAngle fast path; bit-identical (45 seeded matches hashed per tick, every tick rate), botThink -15 to -18%
commitsSinceProduction.author: claude

commitsSinceProduction.subject: Snapshot encode: exact roundHalfAway instead of libm round / lround / remainder in the quantizers (checked over all 2^32 floats, same wire bytes); world encode -50%, snapbench sends -4 to -18%
commitsSinceProduction.author: claude

commitsSinceProduction.subject: Server wait loop: with humans on, sleep on a timer alone until a measured spin before the tick, then spin in idle() (no recv per pass, no wake per input packet: same game); Linux: 1 ns timer slack, recvmmsg / sendmmsg; --tick-spin auto|N; status shows the spin and tick lateness
commitsSinceProduction.author: claude

commitsSinceProduction.subject: UI test: the demo is held only once it has reached its first snapshot (held from the start it only crept on between the hold and the frame's network read, and at CI's ~60 fps it never got there: the demo scenario's setup failed on Linux)
commitsSinceProduction.author: claude

commitsSinceProduction.subject: CI tests as a testing build: quark_tests pins the build to production (testingBuild(), governor.h) since CI builds it as a -test. version on testing, where ranked is never rated (the ranked, race, server and governor groups failed there; a new check covers the testing case); the bot grapple test waits up to 90 s for its first latch (about one in 30 s, so a fixed 30 s sometimes saw none, the build before 1.18.0 too); the UI test's demo setup says which step failed
commitsSinceProduction.author: claude

commitsSinceProduction.subject: 1.18.0 full changelog: the versions.txt line endings fix
commitsSinceProduction.author: claude

commitsSinceProduction.subject: versions.txt written in binary mode: Windows wrote \r\n line endings, so the same file differed by OS (the edit test group failed on Windows)
commitsSinceProduction.author: claude

commitsSinceProduction.subject: 1.18.0: changelogs (short and full) and release checklist rows for Latent Sync, F3 / F4, MAX FPS, GPU MAX CLOCKS and the late mouse read
commitsSinceProduction.author: claude

commitsSinceProduction.subject: MAX FPS is a slider (type or drag any cap, 0 = unlimited, right-click = the screen's refresh rate); Latent Sync is the default present mode on Windows (no vsync elsewhere) and runs unsynced while frames take over 90% of a refresh (tears instead of stuttering); the UI test runs unpaced
commitsSinceProduction.author: claude

commitsSinceProduction.subject: F3 vsync flips: the frames-queue-one-a-blank model only when the game runs at the refresh rate, and at most two blanks behind; faster (the driver keeps the newest, fast sync) a frame flips at its own first blank (the held time grew without end)
commitsSinceProduction.author: claude

commitsSinceProduction.subject: F3 measures vsync: each frame's flip is the first vertical blank (from the monitor's scanline) after the GPU finished it and after the frame before it flipped, shown as VSYNC: HELD FOR ITS BLANK instead of a half-refresh estimate; F4 calibrates the GPU clock itself (it relied on F3 having been open)
commitsSinceProduction.author: claude

commitsSinceProduction.subject: Latent Sync times itself: the finished frame is held and flipped as the vertical blank begins (the tear line stays in the blank whatever the frame took), and frames start early enough for the slowest frame of the last few seconds (input read to GPU done) + 100 us, easing down after 3 s without one; F3 shows the hold
commitsSinceProduction.author: claude

commitsSinceProduction.subject: Latent Sync present mode (Windows): one frame a refresh, flipped as the vertical blank begins (scanline from D3DKMTGetScanLine) so the tear line is off screen, input read as late as the frame's learnt CPU + GPU time allows, tear line offset slider; GPU MAX CLOCKS (NVIDIA: Prefer maximum performance in quark's driver profile via NVAPI DRS); EXCLUSIVE AUDIO moved beside it (it ran off the left column, UI test)
commitsSinceProduction.author: claude

commitsSinceProduction.subject: Fix a heap corruption at thread exit: the per-thread rules cache (Tuned) is allocated once per thread and never freed; as a thread_local object its destructor ran on memory MinGW's emutls had already freed (the UI test's exit 127 crash, and the modes test group's)
commitsSinceProduction.author: claude

commitsSinceProduction.subject: Shadow map before the late latch: the dynamic geometry upload and the shadow pass (Renderer::prepareScene) run before the late mouse read (ULTRA: flushed so the GPU draws the shadow map meanwhile); after the read only the view's draws remain (player shadows measured 74 us of mouse to photon after the read)
commitsSinceProduction.author: claude

commitsSinceProduction.subject: HUD before the late latch: the HUD, F3 / F4 and the 2D upload are built before the late mouse read, so only the world draw and one 2D draw call sit between the read and the swap (~87 us off mouse to photon at 4000 fps); screen-placed HUD bits use the aim from before the read (owner: the UI may lag the aim)
commitsSinceProduction.author: claude

commitsSinceProduction.subject: F4: only the F3 graph's mouse to photon number (same measuring, none of F3's text or bars drawn) to see what the full overlay costs; VOTE START moves from F4 to F5 (bind_version 3 moves it in saved configs)
commitsSinceProduction.author: claude

commitsSinceProduction.subject: Late latch: re-read the mouse and rebuild the view just before the world is drawn (own view, every low-latency mode); the view model is carried to the new aim at draw time, culling is padded ~3.5 degrees; F3 graph measures the wait up to that read
commitsSinceProduction.author: claude

commitsSinceProduction.subject: F3 graph: the mouse's rate as the highest standard poll rate seen (125 Hz x 2^n, counted from 10% under it)
commitsSinceProduction.author: claude

commitsSinceProduction.subject: Raw mouse: hold the hidden cursor at the window's centre while captured instead of GLFW's re-centring captured mode; drop motion while the window isn't focused
commitsSinceProduction.author: claude
